correctness.rationale: For positive exponential edge weights, Dijkstra/Richardson exploration has independent cut-edge clocks with rates 1,1,t and almost surely unique parentage. A finite induction over 289 reachable depth states computes the exact length-3/5/7 rational functions; a second 265-state Boolean ancestry recursion checks length-3 probability. Exact symbolic cancellation verifies all numerator/denominator polynomials and the derivative -(t-1)R(t)/positive_denominator, with R all-positive coefficients. Exhaustive genealogical expansion enumerates 7368 event histories and agrees at six exact rational values. The unique optimum at t=1 follows from strict positive R(t). No extrapolation from finite parameter samples is made; t is quantified over all positive reals.

value.rationale: Q3 is the smallest Boolean cube where a first-passage-minimizing antipodal route can take more than graph-distance many edges; Q2 has only 2-edge antipodal simple paths. Thus the exact length distribution is a canonical first nontrivial kinetic benchmark. The unique maximizer identifies equality of coordinate transmission rates as the optimal way to preserve graph-geodesic ancestry in a physical stochastic-growth model, while monotone passage-time improvement upon increasing one rate creates a meaningful speed–directness tradeoff. This is not merely a known asymptotic bound evaluated at a small parameter.
